item.title: Okawachiyama: The Secret Kiln Village — Guide
item.description: Okawachiyama, tucked into a steep, misty mountain valley above Imari, is one of the most atmospheric pottery towns in Japan. In the Edo period this was the secret village of the Nabeshima kilns, where the ruling lords of the domain sequestered their finest potters to produce Nabeshima ware — porcelain of the highest quality, made exclusively as gifts for the shogun and imperial court, its techniques closely guarded. Cut off by the surrounding mountains to protect these trade secrets, the village retains a wonderfully preserved atmosphere: a narrow lane winds uphill past some thirty working kilns and shops, chimneys rising among the houses, porcelain-tiled bridges and walls, and the potters' cemetery on the slope above.
